**B.** The statute bars force only against a lawful arrest and doesn't remove the right to self-defense against excessive force. On the suspect's account, the officer began beating him with a nightstick over mere cursing, so his punch was justified self-defense and he should be acquitted if the arrest was lawful and the jury believes that account. D fails because on the suspect's account he acted in self-defense whether or not the arrest was lawful, so guilt doesn't follow regardless of account.

CONFIDENCE: 85
